title: parse('next friday') returns today on a Friday
body: Called on Friday 8 May, parse('next friday') gives 8 May. `next` should never mean today, so I expected 15 May.

title: Duration.from_iso rejects weeks combined with days
body: Duration.from_iso('P1W2D') raises ValueError: unexpected designator 'D'. ISO 8601-2 allows weeks with other units.

title: Every-other-week schedule moves an hour after the clock change
body: Schedule('every 2 weeks on monday at 09:00', tz='Europe/Lisbon') yields 10:00 for every date after 29 March.

title: format_relative says 'in 0 days' for later today
body: format_relative(now + 3 hours) returns 'in 0 days'. It should say 'in 3 hours'.

title: Document the strict flag of parse
body: The README mentions parse(..., strict=True) once but never says what it rejects.

title: parse accepts 30 February
body: parse('2026-02-30') returns 2 March instead of raising, with strict=True as well.

title: Schedule.between is slow for minute rules over a year
body: Schedule('every minute').between(jan_1, dec_31) takes 40 s because it steps one occurrence at a time.

title: Accept 'fortnight' as a duration unit
body: parse_duration('1 fortnight') raises. The unit is common in UK timetables and could mean 14 days.

title: Make 'next <weekday>' skip today
body: When today matches, `next` means the same weekday a week later.

diff:
--- a/brindle/parse.py
+++ b/brindle/parse.py
@@ -88,3 +88,3 @@ def next_weekday(start, weekday):
     """The first `weekday` after `start`, never `start` itself."""
-    days = (weekday - start.weekday()) % 7
+    days = (weekday - start.weekday() - 1) % 7 + 1
     return start + timedelta(days=days)

title: Accept W with other ISO designators
Compute biweekly occurrences in local time
body: The rule runs in local time, so 09:00 stays 09:00 after the clock change.

diff:
--- a/brindle/schedules.py
+++ b/brindle/schedules.py
@@ -112,3 +112,4 @@ class Schedule:
     def _occurrence(self, n):
-        at = self.anchor + n * self.period
-        return at.astimezone(self.tz)
+        local = self.anchor.astimezone(self.tz).replace(tzinfo=None)
+        at = local + n * self.period
+        return at.replace(tzinfo=self.tz)

message: Validate the day against the month's length
diff:
--- a/brindle/parse.py
+++ b/brindle/parse.py
@@ -140,2 +140,4 @@ def _date(year, month, day, strict):
     """The date, or InvalidDate for one the calendar does not have."""
-    return date(year, month, 1) + timedelta(days=day - 1)
+    if not 1 <= day <= calendar.monthrange(year, month)[1]:
+        raise InvalidDate(f"{year}-{month:02d} has no day {day}")
+    return date(year, month, day)

title: Use hours for same-day relative times

message: Count hours within the same day
diff:
--- a/brindle/formatting.py
+++ b/brindle/formatting.py
@@ -22,2 +22,5 @@ def format_relative(then, now=None):
     delta = then - (now or datetime.now(then.tzinfo))
+    if abs(delta) < timedelta(days=1):
+        hours = round(abs(delta).total_seconds() / 3600)
+        return f"in {hours} hours" if delta > timedelta(0) else f"{hours} hours ago"
     days = delta.days

title: Explain strict mode in the README
body: A short section with examples of what strict mode rejects.

diff:
--- a/README.md
+++ b/README.md
@@ -34,2 +34,10 @@ parse("next friday")
 ```
+
+### Strict mode
+
+`parse(text, strict=True)` rejects what the default mode guesses at:
+
+- a date the calendar does not have, such as 30 February
+- a two-digit year
+- a weekday that contradicts the date, such as "Monday 12 May 2026"

--- a/brindle/durations.py
+++ b/brindle/durations.py
@@ -12,3 +12,4 @@ UNITS = {
     "day": timedelta(days=1),
     "week": timedelta(weeks=1),
+    "fortnight": timedelta(weeks=2),
 }

title: Duration repr drops zero units
body: repr(Duration(days=1, hours=0)) prints 'Duration(days=1)', while str() prints '1 day 0 hours'. They should agree.
